caption: Figure E6-2, the eight diode schematic symbols; the exam asks only for the Schottky. All eight are horizontal two-lead devices built on a filled triangle against a cathode bar. 1 = varactor-style (a bowed line sweeps across the triangle, bulging toward the cathode); 2 = bidirectional back-to-back pair (two triangles point-to-point at a capped central bar); 3 = Zener-style (angled wings bent at both ends of the cathode bar); 4 = plain junction diode; 5 = LED (two small arrows pointing away up-right - light leaving); 6 = Schottky (the cathode bar ends bend back in squared S-hooks: the top steps left then down, the bottom steps right then up); 7 = point-contact-style device (the diode inside a circle, an angled whisker lead leaving the cathode bar out the upper right); 8 = a circle enclosing two opposed diodes plus the same whisker. The keyed answer: E6B10 (Schottky diode) is symbol 6. The distractors are well chosen - 1, 2, and 3 also carry 'something extra on the cathode bar', so drill the tell: only the Schottky has the pair of squared S-hooks curling back at BOTH bar ends. Redrawn from the NCVEC pool figure.

spoken: Eight diode symbols in two rows of four, numbered 1 to 8 beneath. Each is a filled triangle pointing into a vertical cathode bar with leads left and right, with variations. Number 1 adds a curved bow sweeping across the triangle near the cathode - the varactor-style symbol. Number 2 shows two triangles point to point sharing a central bar with small caps - a bidirectional pair. Number 3 has angled wings bent off both ends of the cathode bar - the Zener. Number 4 is the plain junction diode. Number 5, the LED, has two small arrows leaving upward to the right - light emitted. Number 6, the Schottky, has squared S-shaped hooks curling back at both ends of the cathode bar. Number 7 puts the diode inside a circle with an angled whisker lead from the cathode bar out the upper right - a point-contact-style device. Number 8 encloses two opposed diodes, one pointing right above the axis and one pointing left below, in a circle with the same whisker. The exam keys the Schottky diode to number 6.
